Article Title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
Article Text:
Amit Shah said migration from 40 villages along the China border has stopped, with population rising amid improved facilities and employment opportunities

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday reached out to Arunachal Pradesh amid protests over a proposed dam project, saying the population in 40 villages bordering China has increased and migration has stopped, citing improved employment, healthcare and other facilities. He made the remarks at a cooperative conference in the state, where he also announced development projects under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme.Shah said the Centre has directed the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) to procure produce from local cooperatives in border villages instead of sourcing it from cities, strengthening ties between residents and security forces.“I reviewed this yesterday. I am pleased that people have begun returning to all 40 villages (bordering with China), the population there has increased, and migration has stopped. Electricity, employment, and health facilities have been discussed. Water has also been delivered to the hilltops. The Home Ministry has strictly mandated that the ITBP and the Army should not procure their produce from Tezpur or Guwahati; they must be procured from villages and cooperatives,” news agency ANI quoted Shah as saying.“Women in Arunachal Pradesh are supplying dairy products, eggs, vegetables, millets and flour through their cooperatives, bringing prosperity to rural households and transforming local agriculture and strengthening the relationship between villages and the army,” he added.He said employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family should be the key priorities for Arunachal Pradesh's development. He urged cooperative institutions and women's self-help groups (SHGs) to work towards making the state self-reliant in essential food products.“Every cooperative institution and women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) should take up the challenge of making Arunachal Pradesh self-reliant in essential food products. Employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family must be the four key priorities of Arunachal Pradesh's development,” Shah said.He also assured Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister of the Centre's support for development projects, saying the government would open all avenues for the state's progress.“Yesterday, we discussed in detail all the steps of Arunachal's development for about three and a half to four hours, decided the roadmaps for the future, and made some decisions. Kiren Rijiju and I have taken note of things where the central government’s help is needed. I want to assure Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister that the central government will open all avenues for the development of Arunachal without any delay. Mobile Medical Units were dispatched today to villages in 11 border districts under the Vibrant Village Programme,” he said.Shah also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's decision to reframe border villages as the country's first villages rather than its last, saying they have the right to development.“Vibrant Village Programme was made for villages in border states. Earlier it was called the country’s last village; Narendra Modi changed the concept and awarded the title of the first village in the country. The biggest right to development is of the border villages of the country,” the Union minister said.Shah on Sunday launched 199 development projects worth Rs 110.95 crore under the Vibrant Villages Programme across 11 border districts of Arunachal Pradesh. He also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047, a blueprint outlining the sector's development over the coming decades.Earlier on Saturday, Shah chaired a high-level review meeting in Itanagar to discuss law and order, internal security, border management and development in Arunachal Pradesh.He also reviewed border security and strategic infrastructure along Arunachal Pradesh's approximately 1,126-km international border with China, given its strategic sensitivity.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said migration from 40 villages along the China border has stopped, with population rising amid improved facilities and employment opportunities. He made the remarks at a cooperative conference in the state, where he also announced development projects under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme.

Article Title: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China’s support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
Article Text:
The US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan

Defence expert says report raises questions for Washington

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Political reactions have poured in after a US congressional commission flagged China’s military support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission said China’s military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict complicated India’s operational planning and tied down its military resources, without Beijing directly entering the fighting.The commission, established by the US Congress in 2000, said China views India as a potential competitor and is working to constrain its rise. It warned that Beijing’s growing military partnership with Pakistan has made a possible two-front conflict a greater concern for New Delhi.“China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India’s rise across multiple domains,” the report said.“May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India’s concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop,” the report added.The assessment by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) has drawn reactions from political leaders, with Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi saying the findings were unsurprising, while Congress leader Shama Mohamed questioned Washington’s own policy towards India and Pakistan.Reacting to the report, Chaturvedi said China had itself acknowledged that Pakistan was using Chinese-supplied equipment and defence systems during the operation.She said successive Indian governments, regardless of political affiliation, had sought to manage national security concerns in their dealings with China, and that the report served as another reminder for India to remain cautious.Chaturvedi said India-China trade ties were important, but warned that the money generated through trade could also be used by Beijing in ways that ran counter to India’s national interests.Congress leader Shama Mohamed said China’s support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor was already known and pointed to unresolved tensions along the India-China border, saying the two countries had not returned to the pre-2020 status quo.Mohamed also questioned the US approach towards India, citing the tariff dispute, pressure over Russian oil purchases and President Donald Trump’s meeting with Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir at the White House.“If the US needs India, it has to work with India and keep Pakistan at a distance,” she said, adding that Washington should take India’s security concerns into account while dealing with the region.She also accused the Indian government of failing to prevent China’s growing presence along the border, including in areas near Arunachal Pradesh.Brigadier Hemant Mahajan (retd) said the report was not a major revelation but raised questions about what Washington knew, what it would do in response and how its claims could be independently verified.Mahajan alleged that Chinese support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor extended beyond supplying weapons and included intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, repairs and technical assistance. He claimed that Chinese satellite capabilities and equipment had been used to support Pakistan’s military preparedness.He also alleged that China had provided Pakistan with substantial military equipment and helped repair platforms that had been out of service before the operation. Mahajan said the support had stopped short of China directly joining the conflict.However, he argued that the performance of Chinese-made weapons during the conflict had raised questions about their effectiveness, and said Indian-made systems had performed better. These assessments were his own.Mahajan further questioned whether the US report would lead to any change in Washington’s policy towards China and Pakistan, saying the broader strategic implications of Beijing’s military assistance extended beyond South Asia.
Article Summary: US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan. Political reactions have poured in after a US congressional commission flagged China’s military support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi said the findings were unsurprising, while Congress leader Shama Mohamed questioned Washington's own policy.

Article Title: Jawan hit by own gun, friendly fire during op to get war pension: SC
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh heard the case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not necessary for Army personnel to be hit by an enemy's bullet in order to be entitled to pension under War Injury Element, Supreme Court ruled Friday, ordering that pension be granted even in a case where a soldier is injured in accidental firing from his own gun or his own troops during an operation.A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh said that the order specifically mentioned that Army personnel would be classified as 'Wounded Battle Casualty' in such cases and the grievously injured soldier would be entitled to the pension.The court said the Army order contemplated two situations: a gunshot or splinter injury suffered 'accidentally', or such an injury caused by firing by own troops. "In either situation, the injury must have been sustained while carrying out operations against the enemy or militants. The present case rests on the first limb, 'sustained accidentally'," SC said."A service weapon may discharge without an intention to cause bodily injury to himself, for example, while holding a weapon, an impact or fall, snagging of the trigger, inadvertent pressure on the trigger, or a mechanical defect... These nature of incidents are clearly distinguishable from the idea of self-inflicted injury, which has a certain element of knowledge or intention so as to disqualify from getting enhanced pensionary benefit," the bench said.SC allowed the plea of Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh who got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K when his weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein. It made him 40% disabled and he was granted an ordinary Disability Element of pension. He sought an enhanced pension under War Injury Element. SC quashed the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim. Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K. His weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein.

Article Title: Murders, kidnappings, extortion: Lawrence Bishnoi aide Goldy Brar on FBI's 10 most wanted fugitive list
Article Text:
FBI adds Goldy Brar to ten Most Wanted Fugitives list over alleged transnational crimes

What the FBI alleges against Goldy Brar

Operation Hardball and US action against crime syndicates

Canada announces separate $250,000 reward

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FBI warns public not to approach fugitive

The FBI has added Satinderjeet Singh, alias Goldy Brar, to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and announced a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. Brar is accused of being a North American leader of the Lawrence Bishnoi Organised Crime Group (OCG), a transnational criminal network allegedly involved in murders, extortion, drug trafficking and other violent offences across the United States and Canada.The move comes amid a coordinated effort by US and Canadian law enforcement agencies to track down Brar. On November 19, Canada announced a separate reward of up to $250,000 for information leading to his arrest and named him the number-one suspect on the Bolo Program’s new list of the country’s 25 most wanted fugitives.Also read - Canada announces $250,000 reward for Goldy Brar, names him country's most-wanted fugitive According to the FBI, Brar is wanted in connection with multiple federal offences, including racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to interfere with and attempted interference with commerce by extortion, and conspiracy to distribute and possess controlled substances with intent to distribute. He is also accused of helping direct the activities of the Bishnoi enterprise across several countries.“Satinderjeep Singh, also known as Goldy Brar, is a dangerous individual, and the FBI and our partners have made it our priority to apprehend him, which is why we’re adding him to the FBI’s list of Top Ten fugitives and offering a reward of up to $1 million dollars for his capture,” said FBI Los Angeles Field Office Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy.“The amount of attention this list will bring to his face and description cannot be overstated; his photo will be found on every FBI-affiliated website and social media platform, and will be publicized on every phone around the world until he’s caught.”According to the indictment, Brar was among the trusted lieutenants of Lawrence Bishnoi, who is accused of running a criminal enterprise from prison in India. The indictment alleges that Bishnoi used contraband mobile phones and internet-based communication devices to direct criminal activities, while delegating operational responsibilities to associates, including Brar.The FBI describes the Bishnoi enterprise as a transnational network involved in targeted killings, shootings, kidnappings, extortion, assaults and the trafficking of narcotics and weapons. The group allegedly used violence and online publicity surrounding its criminal activities to create fear and extort victims, particularly in India and among Indian diaspora communities.One of the cases cited in the indictment concerns the killing of a prominent political and religious figure from Punjab who was living in Canada. Identified in court documents as “H.S.N.”, the individual was shot dead by two gunmen as he left a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia, on June 18, 2023.The indictment alleges that Bishnoi and Brar ordered the assassination. The allegations are part of the US federal case against the accused.The indictment also alleges that members of the Bishnoi enterprise stole approximately 520 kg of cocaine from rival drug trafficking gangs in the greater Los Angeles area between March 2024 and July 2025.Brar's addition to the FBI list follows the July 7 announcement of Operation Hardball, a years-long federal investigation into India-based transnational organised crime groups. The US Attorney's Office announced the unsealing of three indictments charging 37 defendants with offences linked to three such groups.The alleged crimes included racketeering, targeted killings, shootings, extortion and the international trafficking of large quantities of narcotics. One of the indictments focused on the Bishnoi enterprise.“The inclusion of this defendant on the FBI’s Top Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list underscores this administration’s determination to bring the full force of the law upon transnational criminal gangs,” said First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli.“Working together with law enforcement in Canada, Europe, and Asia, we will continue to hunt down thugs such as ‘Goldy Brar’ and ensure they never see the outside of a prison again.”At the time of the Operation Hardball announcement, 24 of the federal defendants had been arrested or were already in custody. Authorities said four other fugitives had been captured and one had been confirmed dead. The FBI said it continued to search for five fugitives, including Brar.A day before the latest FBI-related coverage, on November 19, the Winnipeg Police Service announced a reward of up to $250,000 for information leading to Brar's arrest in Canada or the United States. The reward will remain active until November 2, 2027.Brar is wanted under a Canada-wide warrant for first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in connection with the September 20, 2023, killing of 39-year-old Sukhdool Singh Gill, also known as Sukha Duneke, in Winnipeg.Canadian authorities said arrest warrants were issued on February 23, 2026, for Brar and another suspect, 26-year-old Karanbir Singh, who faces the same charges. Both remain at large.“We will aggressively defend our cities, and our country, against this kind of violence,” said Winnipeg Deputy Chief Cam Mackid in a statement. “We don’t accept it, and we will be relentless.”The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) also welcomed Brar's addition to the FBI's list.“Goldy Brar and his network have wreaked devastating havoc on countless lives—through high-profile murders, shootings, death threats, extortion, arson, and drug trafficking,” said Lisa Moreland, the deputy commissioner of federal policing for the RCMP.“His addition to the FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list speaks to the collective resolve to capture him. The RCMP is committed to continue working with partners in the FBI to bring Goldy Brar to justice.”The FBI has described Brar as extremely violent, armed and dangerous. It said he is known to reside in California and various parts of Canada and warned members of the public against approaching him.Anyone with information about his whereabouts can contact the FBI's toll-free tip line at 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324), approach their local FBI office or the nearest US embassy or consulate, or submit information through the agency's online tip portal. The FBI said tips can be provided anonymously.The case is being investigated by the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office, the Los Angeles Police Department and the RCMP, with assistance from domestic and international law enforcement partners.
Article Summary: FBI has added Satinderjeet Singh, alias Goldy Brar, to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and announced a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. Brar is accused of being a North American leader of the Lawrence Bishnoi Organised Crime Group (OCG), a transnational criminal network allegedly involved in murders, extortion, drug trafficking and other violent offences.

Article Title: 'Rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi': Sanjay Raut's demand amid Dadar Metro renaming row
Article Text:
File photo of Sanjay Raut

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Friday demanded that Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar, amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'Chaityabhoomi'.Raut urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis to bring a proposal to rename Nagpur, saying his party would extend its support even if the move faced opposition."Dadar is just a station. The biggest honour to Dr Ambedkar would be to change Nagpur's name to Deekshabhoomi. The chief minister should bring a proposal and we will support it," Raut told reporters.He said Deekshabhoomi held immense historical significance as the site where Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956, marking a turning point in the movement against caste discrimination."Social revolution in Dr Ambedkar's life began at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. We will stand by the government on this if any conflict arises on the issue," he added.The demand also found support from the Congress, with legislature party leader Vijay Wadettiwar questioning why Nagpur could not be renamed after the historic site."The name (of Nagpur) should be changed to Deekshabhoomi. What is the problem in changing the name to Deekshabhoomi?" Wadettiwar said.He credited Ambedkar with framing a Constitution that protects India's democracy and said Deekshabhoomi attracts visitors from across the world.The BJP, however, criticised Raut over his demand and accused Shiv Sena (UBT) of opposing the proposed renaming of Dadar Metro station.Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders were using the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) as a proxy to oppose the government's move. He said Raut should first welcome the decision to rename the Metro station as Chaityabhoomi."He (Raut) never goes to Chaityabhoomi, nor does he propagate Dr Ambedkar's thoughts. Such people have no right to speak on the issue," Ban said.Maharashtra minister and senior BJP leader Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Nagpur was already widely associated with Deekshabhoomi."Every person who comes to Nagpur goes to Deekshabhoomi," he said.This comes after Fadnavis announced the state government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station as Chaityabhoomi, subject to completion of the necessary procedures.The announcement had initially caused confusion over whether the proposed name change concerned Dadar railway station. The chief minister's Office subsequently clarified that the proposal applied only to the Metro station and that the suburban railway station would retain its existing name.The renaming proposal has drawn political reactions, with the MNS raising objections to changing Dadar's name.Both Chaityabhoomi and Deekshabhoomi are closely associated with Ambedkar's life and legacy.On October 14, 1956, Ambedkar converted to Buddhism along with hundreds of thousands of followers at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. The event became a defining moment in the Dalit Buddhist movement.Ambedkar died on December 6, 1956, and was cremated at Chaityabhoomi in Mumbai's Dadar area.Both sites attract large numbers of followers every year, particularly during Dhammachakra Pravartan Din in Nagpur and Mahaparinirvan Diwas in Mumbai.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut demands Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar. Demand comes amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'ChaityabhoomI'

Article Title: Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb on wish list as Pakistan minister visits India; what Centre said on travel curbs
Article Text:
Taj Mahal on Pakistan minister's wish list

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik expressed a desire to visit some of India's heritage sites, including the iconic Taj Mahal . Malik attended the SCO meeting in New Delhi as part of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government.His visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India since then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's high-profile visit in 2023 for the SCO meeting.Accompanied by his wife and a senior Pakistani official, Malik spoke about his interest in exploring India beyond the multilateral engagement. Both are visiting India for the first time.Asked whether he planned to visit the Taj Mahal and explore other parts of the country, Malik said he hoped to meet people and see some places if his schedule allowed."I have come to India for a few days. Tomorrow I will be engaged due to the SCO forum. I may not be able to explore much this time, but whatever opportunity I will get, I will try to meet people also and see some places, and understand them. People are the same everywhere," he said.The Centre, meanwhile, denied imposing any restrictions on the movement of Malik or other ministers attending the event. Official sources said all visiting ministers were free to travel anywhere in the country, including the Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb.However, security considerations may have affected the possibility of Malik visiting the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah.Speaking on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the historic Purana Qila, Malik was also asked whether the multilateral engagement could help improve India-Pakistan relations He said he had come to India for discussions in a multilateral context, while underlining the importance of cultural exchanges in bringing people and countries closer."This forum is itself multilateral. You should engage in multilateral discussions. Even the questions you have asked today have not been bilateral; everything here is happening in a multilateral context. We have also come here for multilateral discussions," he said.Amid continued unease in bilateral ties following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , which claimed 26 lives, Malik said culture had a "key role" to play in fostering dialogue between the two countries.He stressed that cultural engagement was not limited to bilateral relations but had wider regional significance, adding that greater understanding between people was essential for the region's progress."Unless we understand each other, our way of thinking and manners of living, we won't be able to grow. Through dialogues, we will get each other's perspectives and get to know each other's understanding, and that's how the region will be able to grow," the Pakistan minister said.India-Pakistan ties deteriorated further in April 2025 after Pakistan-backed terrorists killed 26 people in an attack in south Kashmir's Pahalgam. India responded by launching counterterror Operation Sindoor , a military operation targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in 2025 following the Pahalgam attack, among a series of measures taken against Pakistan.
Article Summary: Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik expressed a desire to visit some of India's heritage sites. Malik attended the SCO meeting in New Delhi as part of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government. His visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India since then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's visit in 2023.

Article Title: ‘Bitten by dogs’: Revanth Reddy’s swipe at dissenting MLAs sparks row in Telangana Congress
Article Text:
Reddy recalled an old saying that shortcomings should be discussed privately while achievements should be highlighted publicly.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy 's remarks taking a swipe at critics within his own party have sparked a row amid growing signs of dissent in the state Congress.Addressing a public gathering in Siddipet on November 19, Reddy accused some party members of publicly highlighting the government's shortcomings while privately praising its work. He said his government still had two years in office and invited people to flag unfinished work and pending demands.“Today, I want to tell you just one thing. Our government has two years. If there is anything that hasn't been done, tell us. If there is anything that needs to be done, tell us. And if there is good that we have done, tell the whole town about it,” he said, news agency ANI reported.Taking an apparent dig at some party colleagues, he recalled an old saying that shortcomings should be discussed privately while achievements should be highlighted publicly.“Yesterday and the day before, some of our own people- I don't know what happened to them; maybe a mad dog bit them- have been saying all the bad things on the mic, and coming to my house to whisper the good things in my ear. There will be some mad people like this, people bitten by a mad dog...” Reddy said.The remarks come against the backdrop of growing discontent within the Telangana Congress , nearly three years after the party came to power. Criticism of the chief minister is increasingly emerging from within the ruling party, including sitting MLAs, MPs, ministers and sections of its original leadership.The latest flashpoint involved Munugode MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy, who accused the state government of discriminating against constituencies represented by legislators outside the chief minister's immediate political circle.He alleged that development funds were being preferentially allocated to Kodangal, Reddy's constituency, and areas represented by ministers, while other MLAs were struggling to secure funds for basic development works.He also warned of another political “Kurukshetra” over the alleged discrimination.
Article Summary: Revanth Reddy accused some party members of publicly highlighting the government's shortcomings while privately praising its work. He said his government still had two years in office and invited people to flag unfinished work and pending demands. The remarks come against the backdrop of growing discontent within the Telangana Congress.

Article Title: NGT scanner on waste dumping near J&K’s saffron fields
Article Text:
The National Green Tribunal has directed an expert committee to evaluate environmental damage in Pampore.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: National Green Tribunal (NGT) has constituted a committee of experts to assess environmental damage and inspect a municipal dumping site in J&K’s Pampore after an activist filed a petition alleging such waste disposals were threatening the area’s vast saffron fields.The NGT division bench of Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Afroz Ahmad directed the committee to submit a report in eight weeks. The order, passed recently, comes at a time when saffron cultivation has fallen nearly 35% over the years, posing serious challenges for farmers. Saffron, locally known as kesar, is believed to have originated in southern Europe but is now widely cultivated in Iran, Spain and Turkey. In India, it is primarily grown in Pampore.The NGT-formed panel will include representatives of Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), to be nominated by its vice-chancellor, regional director of the Union environment ministry and a nominee of the J&K Pollution Control Committee.The members visit the Pampore site, in Pulwama district, find out the extent of municipal and plastic waste dumped there and ascertain if necessary clearances have been secured.“The committee will also ascertain the effect of dumping of the waste upon the crop,” the order states.In his NGT plea, environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat has alleged that Pampore’s municipal body was illegally dumping harmful materials at its solid waste management facility in Patlibagh-Galander area.Untreated waste was generating leachate that was seeping into underground water sources and flowing through channels into the Jhelum river, located less than 1km away, Bhat’s plea says.The dumping site is located in a notified saffron-growing area protected under Saffron Act, 2007, attracting rodents and porcupines which further damage crops, Bhat’s plea says. He submitted with his petition a report by the local pollution control officer about “heaps of unsegregated and untreated waste, including single-use plastic items and packaging materials”. “Apart from this site, they are using saffron fields for dumping municipal waste,” Bhat told TOI.Saffron cultivation has declined around 35% from 5,707 hectares in early 2000s to 3,715 hectares a decade later. Productivity also plunged. However, govt says the decline has been checked since 2010-11 when a Rs 400-crore Saffron Mission was started. Farmers dispute the claim.
Article Summary: The National Green Tribunal has directed an expert committee to evaluate environmental damage in Pampore. An activist filed a petition alleging such waste disposals were threatening the area’s vast saffron fields. The NGT division bench of Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Afroz Ahmad directed the committee to submit a report in eight weeks.

Article Title: Ladakh records 70% voting in panchayat polls, 52% in municpal elections
Article Text:
Ladakh recorded a voter turnout of 70.03 percent in the panchayat elections and 52.4 percent in municipal polls.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Ladakh Saturday recorded 70.03% turnout in panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal council polls, held for the first time since it was declared a Union Territory in 2019.The young and the elderly, women and men, first-time voters, monks and people from every walk of life exercised their democratic right across villages and towns. The state election commission said the enthusiastic participation reflected the people’s deep commitment to grassroots democracy and local self-governance.The local body polls were held amid protests led by Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) seeking deferment of Dec 4 elections to eight autonomous hill development councils, citing the harsh winter.The panchayat elections covered 192 Panchayat Halqas across eight districts, comprising 192 sarpanch positions and 1,428 panch seats. Of these, 55 sarpanches and 1,186 panches were elected unopposed, while polling was conducted for the remaining 137 sarpanch and 242 panch seats.The municipal council elections covered 38 wards, comprising 21 in Leh and 17 in Kargil. Polling was conducted in all 21 wards of Leh, while four wards in Kargil were filled unopposed and polling was held in the remaining 13 wards.Election authorities had made elaborate arrangements for the smooth conduct of polling. In Zanskar, helicopters were deployed to airlift polling teams to three remote and road-inaccessible polling stations, enabling the conduct of elections in some of the most isolated settlements.Ladakh lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena described the day as historic for the region, saying the overwhelming participation in the polls “is a powerful testament to people’s unshakeable faith in the democratic process and local self-governance”.However, LAB co-chairperson Chering Dorjay Lakrook and member Sonam Wangchuk alleged at a joint press conference in Leh that a “large number of people” had been left out of the electoral rolls. “I wanted to go to my own village to vote but I was told that the polling booth there had been shifted to another village. That is why villagers in my village boycotted the polls,” Wangchuk said.Wangchuk, who stepped out of his house Saturday after the administration withdrew the security cordon around it, accused the administration of “behaving like a rogue state” and alleged that elections were being imposed on the people of Ladakh.The administration’s alleged “anti-Ladakh measures” were fuelling anger among the people, he said, warning that the growing resentment would have serious implications for national security.The strategically important region “should not be left at the mercy of administrators who behave like a bull in a china shop”, the climate activist said, urging the prime minister and the defence minister to intervene and ensure that the people of Ladakh got their due.
Article Summary: Ladakh recorded a voter turnout of 70.03 percent in the panchayat elections and 52.4 percent in municipal polls. The state election commission said the enthusiastic participation reflected the people’s deep commitment to grassroots democracy and local self-governance.

Article Title: 'Not about food': Owaisi's response to Azam Khan's 'Hyderabadi biryani' jibe

Owaisi responded to Khan's biryani jibe by citing his visits to Muzaffarnagar riot victims and Akhlaq's family

Article Title: 'Census-related delimitation should be put on hold for 25 years': CPM general secretary MA Baby

CPM general secretary MA Baby (ANI)

NEW DELHI: CPM general secretary MA Baby on Saturday called for a 25-year postponement of census-linked delimitation and criticised the Centre over what he described as a lack of clarity on the start of Parliament's Winter Session "We are demanding that the census-related delimitation should be put on hold for another 25 years," he told news agency ANI.Baby also accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat of keeping political parties and Parliament out of discussions on the matter."Now nothing is known. It is quite possible, then, that they will announce the cancellation of the Winter Session," Congress leader Jairam Ramesh told ANI."They know that if a session is called, every party will raise the issue of the CEC, and they will have no answers," he added.The opposition and civil society groups have been demanding Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The controversy intensified after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised 14 complaints over the past 10 months regarding decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the SIR exercise.The Monsoon Session of Parliament began on July 20 and concluded on August 13, following 19 sittings spread over 25 days. Article Title: 'Voices carry no weight': Wangchuk warns Ladakh's alienation could hurt national security during war
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk warns that alienating people in strategically sensitive Ladakh could have serious national security implications during a conflict.

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday accused the Ladakh administration of treating the Union Territory "like a colony", alleging that decisions were being imposed on people without their consent.Addressing a press conference along with Leh Apex Body chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk, Wangchuk warned that the continued alienation of the strategically sensitive border region could have serious consequences for national security."Ladakh has effectively become a colony where the voices of local people carry no weight and decisions are simply imposed on them. How can such a system continue?" Wangchuk asked."Ladakh has stood with the country during previous wars, and it should continue to do so. Why are such loyal and patriotic people being repeatedly subjected to this treatment?" he said.Warning against alienating people in a strategically sensitive border region, Wangchuk said the consequences of imposing decisions on them might not be immediately apparent during peacetime but could become significant during a conflict."They may not be able to do much in peacetime, but there could be differences in times of war," he said, urging the Centre to ensure that people in Ladakh enjoy the same democratic rights as citizens elsewhere in the country.According to news agency PTI, Wangchuk also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and defence minister Rajnath Singh to intervene, saying the issue should be examined from a national security perspective rather than being left solely to the lieutenant governor's administration or the ministry of home affairs.He also called for an inquiry commission under the Union home ministry to examine the grievances of local government employees and officers and assess their views on the administration's functioning.Wangchuk claimed that even employees belonging to Ladakh were deeply unhappy with the manner in which decisions were being taken.His remarks came amid continuing protests over Ladakh's political and constitutional demands and the ongoing electoral process.Earlier, Wangchuk, a prominent member of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), alleged that around 20-25 police and paramilitary personnel had been stationed outside his residence, restricting his movement.In a video message posted on his social media accounts, including X and Facebook, the activist claimed that security personnel, vehicles and tents had been positioned around his house, with armed personnel deployed on all sides.He alleged that the restrictions were imposed while he and other members of the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) were preparing to stage a sit-in protest over various demands concerning Ladakh.The proposed demonstration was also linked to concerns over the timing of the upcoming elections to the Autonomous Hill Development Councils, scheduled for December 4.The police, however, denied that Wangchuk had been placed under house arrest. The clarification came after the activist alleged that he had been confined to his residence after being taken away from a protest site and escorted home on November 11."Police arrangements which (were) placed to ensure compliance with prohibitory order have been withdrawn," Leh district police said in a post on X.The police further stated that the prohibitory order had been issued by the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) of Leh and denied claims that Wangchuk was under house arrest."ADM Leh has passed a prohibitory order against Shri Sonam Wangchuk. It is clarified that he was not put under any house arrest as has been claimed," the statement said.
Article Summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk accuses Ladakh administration of treating the Union Territory "like a colony" Wangchuk warns that the continued alienation of the strategically sensitive border region could have serious consequences for national security. The police, however, deny that Wangchuk had been placed under house arrest.

Article Title: Watch: Masked ICE agents drag away two at US’ Seattle airport, spark chaos during boarding
Article Text:
Masked ICE agents detain two mid-boarding at US’ Seattle airport, Airlines calls scene ‘distressing’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained two people on a crowded jet bridge at United States' Seattle-Tacoma International Airport while passengers were boarding a Los Angeles-bound flight on Saturday. The incident triggered a chaotic confrontation with passengers after one traveller allegedly threw hot coffee at federal officers.The operation unfolded on Saturday on the jet bridge as passengers were boarding Alaska Airlines Flight 1306, scheduled to depart at 8:10 am for Los Angeles. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said agents carried out a targeted operation at around 8:05 am to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican citizen who had overstayed his visa.According to ICE, other travellers began obstructing and attacking agents as the arrest was under way. The agency alleged that another passenger, identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, threw hot coffee at officers. She was also found to have overstayed her visa and was taken into custody.ICE said Mejia could face charges of assaulting a federal officer, warning that anyone who assaulted or obstructed law enforcement would be prosecuted.“Anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law,” the agency said, citing Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's position.Videos of the confrontation showed masked agents pulling people away as passengers watched. In the footage a woman could be heard crying out that her daughter was being detained and had a work permit. Officers were also seen grappling with a person on the floor.Online flight data showed that the departure was delayed.Alaska Airlines said ICE had not informed it in advance about the enforcement action. “We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306,” the airline said in a statement.“We recognise how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests.”The airline added that it remained committed to “treating every guest with dignity and respect”. It said it was working with the Port of Seattle to determine whether established protocols had been followed and had raised its concerns “directly with the appropriate authorities”.The Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, also described the incident as distressing.In a statement, the port said the episode had affected not only the family involved but also other passengers. It added that local authorities would “engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”.“We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”, the port said.Washington governor Bob Ferguson criticised the enforcement operation, describing ICE's tactics as “deeply un-American” and calling for the agency to be abolished.“The video is horrific and it is chilling,” Ferguson said at an afternoon news conference attended by labour leaders and local elected officials.“We need a system of immigration enforcement and border security that is effective, ethical and humane. And ICE is not it. It is beyond reform.”Ferguson also said he was examining how federal agents accessed the jet bridge. He believed they had violated a state law he signed in March restricting the use of facial coverings by law enforcement officers.ICE has increased enforcement operations at airports since the summer, with particular attention to people suspected of overstaying visas.
Article Summary: Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained two people on a crowded jet bridge at United States' Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Incident triggered a chaotic confrontation with passengers after one traveller allegedly threw hot coffee at federal officers. Alaska Airlines said ICE had not informed it in advance about the enforcement action.

Article Title: Epstein’s Russia obsession: 17 Young women, oligarchs and a desperate bid for redemption
Article Text:
Jeffrey Epstein sought to rebuild his influence in Russia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein continued recruiting women from Russia and other former Soviet states while cultivating ties with wealthy businessmen and senior officials in the country, seeking to restore his standing among the global elite after his 2008 conviction, an investigation has found. At least 17 women from Russia and other former Soviet countries were drawn into this sex-trafficking network.Based on interviews with more than two dozen people familiar with Epstein’s Russian connections and a review of hundreds of pages of documents, news agency Reuters found that Russia was both a source of women drawn into his sex-trafficking network and a potential route back into influential circles.Three of these 17 women, identified in the investigation, later sought justice for his abuse and exploitation.Epstein’s interest in Russia began with its modelling industry. In the years following the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, modelling scouts travelled across the region looking for young talent. French scout Jean-Luc Brunel, who worked with Epstein, recruited women from Eastern Europe and brought them to Paris and the United States, according to people interviewed by Reuters.Former model Thysia Huisman recalled meeting Epstein at a party hosted by Brunel in Paris in September 1991.She said a Russian girl who appeared to be in her early teens spent much of the evening on Epstein’s lap.“The girl said modeling work was not good, but ‘Jeffrey takes care of me,’” Huisman told Reuters. “It was creepy,” she added, recalling the girl’s apparent age. Reuters said it could not independently confirm the party or the identity and age of the girl.Epstein made two known visits to Russia, in 1998 and 2002. The first took him to Sarov, a closed city associated with the Soviet Union’s nuclear weapons programme. His second trip included Moscow and St Petersburg, where he travelled with Brunel and Ghislaine Maxwell , according to flight records and people familiar with the journey.After pleading guilty in Florida in 2008 to prostitution-related charges, including soliciting an underage girl, and serving 13 months in jail, Epstein increasingly sought to cultivate Russian elites, the agency found.His contacts included Russian real-estate tycoon Vladislav Doronin and former deputy economy minister Sergey Belyakov. Emails reviewed by Reuters showed Epstein sought to use Belyakov as a channel to senior Russian leaders.In an April 2015 email to former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak, Epstein wrote, “I suggest you send (Belyakov) a note,” saying Russian president Vladimir Putin and his advisers “would benefit from spending some time with Jeffrey to discuss markets, currency and the financial system”.Reuters found no evidence that Epstein ever met Putin, worked for Russian intelligence or acted on behalf of the Russian government. An apparent effort to arrange a 2011 meeting with Putin was ultimately abandoned, with people familiar with the episode describing the proposed appointment as “a charade”.Epstein’s Russian connections also extended through modelling agencies. Reuters reported that Brunel’s Miami agency, MC2 Models Management, recruited heavily in Russia, while Epstein provided accommodation for some models. One former model, Svetlana Pozhidaeva, told Reuters that Epstein sexually abused her and used financial and immigration arrangements to make her dependent on him.Epstein died in a Manhattan jail in 2019 while facing federal sex-trafficking charges involving minors. However, the report said that efforts to gain influence in Russia produced no major business deals or demonstrable access to Putin. His ties to the country, however, remain part of wider investigations into his trafficking network and the powerful figures who moved within his circle.
Article Summary: At least 17 women from Russia and other former Soviet countries were drawn into this sex-trafficking network. Three of these 17 women, identified in the investigation, later sought justice for his abuse and exploitation. Epstein’s interest in Russia began with its modelling industry.

Article Title: Princeton PhD student, Chinese-born neuroscientist, Eva Yi Xie detained by ICE at airport; DHS says she overstayed visa, lawyers challenge arrest
Article Text:
Chinese-born neuroscientist arrested by ICE at airport on accusation of visa overstay

Who is Eva Yi Xie?

Princeton university arranges legal assistance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What happened before her arrest?

A 24-year-old Princeton University doctoral student has been detained by ICE after she was stopped at an airport while returning from an academic conference in Washington, DC. The Trump administration accused her of overstaying her visa, while her lawyers argued that she was legally allowed to remain in the US because of her pending asylum application. Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience PhD student at Princeton, was detained on November 19 at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Virginia. She had travelled to Washington to attend the Society for Neuroscience's annual conference, where she presented her research.The DHS said ICE had conducted a targeted enforcement operation at the airport to arrest Xie. According to the department, Xie entered the US on March 16, 2016, on a temporary basis and was required to leave by September 15, 2016. DHS alleged that she failed to depart by that date and did not have valid authorisation to study in the country."Xie will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending her removal proceedings," the department said.However, her legal team has disputed the government's position, arguing that Xie has a pending asylum application that allows her to remain in the US while her case is being considered.Xie moved to the US from China in 2016, when she was a minor. She attended the Bronx High School of Science in New York before graduating from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 2024 with degrees in computer science and mathematics.She joined Princeton University in 2024 and is a third-year doctoral candidate at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute. Her research focuses on the neural basis of decision-making, examining how the human brain processes information and makes choices. She is advised by Princeton neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and co-advised by professors Nathaniel Daw and Benjamin Eysenbach.Before joining Princeton, Xie also interned with Meta, Microsoft AI and IBM Research, according to The Daily Princetonian.Why was the Princeton student detained by ICE?Xie's lawyer, Kerry Doyle, told The Daily Princetonian that she was an asylum seeker whose immigration court hearing was scheduled for January 2028. Her family had applied for asylum within a year of arriving in the US, Doyle said. The application was referred to immigration court, where it remains pending. Although Xie's visa had expired, her lawyers claimed that her pending asylum application allowed her to stay in the country. They also said she had valid employment authorization and no criminal history.The lawyers have filed a habeas corpus petition in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, challenging the legality of her detention.According to Doyle, the petition argued that ICE arrested Xie without a warrant and that there were no circumstances suggesting she posed an imminent flight risk or needed to be taken into custody without one.A federal judge ordered ICE not to remove Xie from the Eastern District of Virginia before ruling on the habeas corpus petition. The agency was directed to respond to the petition by Wednesday, November 25.Princeton University confirmed that it had arranged legal representation for Xie following her detention. "News of Eva's detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community," Graduate School Dean Rodney Priestley said in a statement. He added that the university would remain in contact with her legal team, family and colleagues to provide support. "We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton," he said.Her research adviser, Carlos Brody, also appealed for help, describing her as a brilliant scientist, colleague, mentor and friend. "She went to a conference to present her work, and now she's in a detention center. She should be home," he wrote in a social media post.Xie had travelled to Washington to attend the Society for Neuroscience's annual meeting and presented a research poster on November 18. She was reportedly preparing to board a domestic flight to San Francisco when she was detained the following day. A member of her research lab said Xie sent a message to colleagues on Slack asking for help on November 19. They lost contact with her for several hours before managing to reach her again.
Article Summary: Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience PhD student at Princeton, was detained on November 19 at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Virginia. She had travelled to Washington to attend the Society for Neuroscience's annual conference, where she presented her research. The Trump administration accused her of overstaying her visa. Her lawyers argued that she was legally allowed to remain in the US because of her pending asylum application.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu horror: 54-year-old woman raped, murdered inside train coach at Nagercoil; gold ring helps police crack case
Article Text:
The accused Iyappan





KANYAKUMARI: Government Railway Police (GRP) have identified the woman who was raped and murdered inside a train coach at Nagercoil Junction. Her identity was established using the BIS hallmark engraved on her gold ring.Inspector General of Police (Government Railway Police) Abishek Dixit told TOI that the BIS hallmark played a key role in identifying the victim.“We checked the hallmark number and found records showing that the jewellery had been sold by a wholesaler in Gujarat. We contacted the wholesaler, who provided details of the retailer in Madhya Pradesh. The retailer then gave us the original bill along with the PAN card details of the person in whose name the bill was issued,” said Dixit.“Thus, we traced the victim’s address and identified her as Urmila Markam, 52, of Balaghat district in Madhya Pradesh. Her father has been summoned to confirm her identity,” Dixit said.Police said a case had been registered at Malajkhand police station on October 22 following her disappearance. The case was registered under sections relating to kidnapping and murder.On November 18, the victim’s decomposed body was found in the differently-abled coach of the Nagercoil-Kottayam Express at Yard No.13.The case was initially registered as an unnatural death but was later changed to murder under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), after an autopsy revealed severe rib and pelvic fractures caused by a violent assault.Using CCTV footage and intelligence inputs, special teams arrested Iyappan near a bus stand on November 20.Following his confession, Section 64 (rape) of the BNS was added to the case. He was remanded to judicial custody until December 2.
Article Summary: Government Railway Police have identified the woman who was raped and murdered inside a train coach at Nagercoil Junction. Her identity was established using the BIS hallmark engraved on her gold ring. On November 18, the victim’s decomposed body was found in the differently-abled coach of the Nager coil- Kottayam Express at Yard No.13.

Article Title: Auto driver killed as underground fuel tank lid flies off at Coimbatore petrol bunk; 3 employees detained
Article Text:
An auto-rickshaw driver named Kannimuthu was killed by a flying iron lid from an underground fuel storage tank





COIMBATORE: An auto-rickshaw driver was killed after an iron lid of an underground fuel storage tank at a petrol bunk on Mettupalayam Road flew off due to pressure and struck him on Saturday.The deceased was identified as Kannimuthu, a resident of Ramasamy Layout in Peelamedu. He had gone to a petrol bunk near Sanganur Pirivu in Kavundampalayam to fill CNG in his auto-rickshaw.According to police, a new underground tank had been constructed at the petrol station to store fuel, and pipeline connection work was under way. The tank had iron lids at both ends to facilitate the pipeline connections.While workers opened the lid on one side to carry out the installation work, pressure reportedly built up inside the tank, causing the lid at the opposite end to suddenly detach and fly off. Kannimuthu, who was standing near his auto-rickshaw, was struck by the flying lid and sustained severe injuries. He died on the spot.After receiving information about the incident, Kavundampalayam police rushed to the spot, recovered the body and sent it to Coimbatore Medical College Hospital for a postmortem examination.Police registered a case and detained three petrol bunk employees for questioning.Preliminary inquiries revealed that the underground tank had remained covered for nearly two months, potentially allowing pressure to build up inside it. An investigation is under way to establish the exact cause of the accident.
Article Summary: An auto-rickshaw driver was killed after an iron lid of an underground fuel storage tank flew off due to pressure and struck him. The deceased was identified as Kannimuthu, a resident of Ramasamy Layout in Peelamedu.

Article Title: Madhya Pradesh horror: Man held for strangling wife after phone dispute in Balaghat
Article Text:
In Balaghat district, a woman named Sushma Raut was murdered by her husband Dinesh Raut (AI image)





BHOPAL: A quarrel over late-night mobile phone use ended in the murder of a woman in Balaghat district, with her husband accused of strangling her at their home in Siwangaht village.The victim, identified as Sushma Raut, had been married to Dinesh Raut for three years. When Sushma showed no signs of movement for around 10 to 15 minutes, he panicked and called family members, claiming that her health had suddenly deteriorated.He subsequently took her to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead.An argument broke out, during which Dinesh allegedly slapped her. Sushma retaliated with a slap, escalating the dispute.The suspicious circumstances surrounding Sushma’s death led police to question Dinesh. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to killing his wife. Police said he was also known to consume alcohol, and the couple frequently quarrelled.
Article Summary: Sushma Raut was killed by her husband Dinesh Raut in Balaghat district. Police say she was using her mobile phone late on Thursday night, disturbing her husband’s sleep. Article Title: Adani power project in Satara: ‘Nod covers 4 villages, excavation on at 5th’
Article Text:
Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar.





MUMBAI: Amid a row over work on Adani Green Energy Ltd’s (AGEL) 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project beginning in Satara’s Patan taluka despite lack of approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), the state forest department’s honorary wildlife warden for the district has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway in Sawarghar village, which was not listed on the environmental clearance (EC) granted by the Union forest ministry on Feb 11 last year.The honorary wildlife warden, Rohan Bhate, said the EC specified only four villages that stand to be affected—Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu—in the district.A spokesperson from Adani Group said the EC covers the four villages as well as Dafalwadi, and the company later purchased private land in Sawarghar to set up temporary accommodation for workers. The company said such an accommodation was included in the project layout approval from Central Electricity Authority. It said the project has all the relevant clearances and initial works are in progress at the site.The Tarali project, estimated at Rs 5,675 crore, is planned over 150.7 hectares of private land.In his letter to MPCB member-secretary Rahul Rekhawar, Bhate claimed that the activity in Sawarghar did not have the required EC and NBWL’s approval, and sought urgent intervention and an independent investigation.Rekhawar confirmed that MPCB has received Bhate’s letter and said it is investigating the allegations.Amol Satpute, MPCB sub-regional officer in Satara, said a team from the pollution regulator inspected the Sawarghar site on Friday, where excavation was underway. Satpute said when officials questioned the site supervisor, they were told the developer was levelling land to set up a labour camp for the Tarali project. He said a report would be submitted to higher authorities.Bhate said the situation raised questions about the geographical scope and validity of the EC in relation to the work being carried out at Sawarghar. He questioned whether MPCB had verified that the proponent had obtained environmental and wildlife clearances for all land parcels involved before issuing the mandatory ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) that allows construction to begin. He said MPCB cannot distance itself from responsibility because the CTE stage is a crucial regulatory checkpoint.Bhate requested an immediate site inspection and preparation of an official panchnama by MPCB officials to document the extent of excavation and construction, the machinery deployed, and the exact location of the work. He said if any excavation or construction is found to have started without statutory approvals, authorities should register the appropriate offence and initiate legal proceedings against responsible individuals and project authorities.He also asked MPCB to determine whether activity at Sawarghar is covered by the Feb 11, 2025, EC and whether all applicable environmental permissions for that specific location have been obtained. In addition, he sought verification of whether prior approval from the NBWL’s standing committee was secured wherever legally required.Bhate said the proposed project falls within the deemed eco-sensitive zone of Koyna wildlife sanctuary and the Sahyadri tiger reserve, making strict scrutiny under environmental and wildlife protection provisions essential. He requested that the matter be assigned to an impartial higher-level authority for an independent inquiry rather than being examined only by officials linked to project clearances. Pending verification, he asked for directions to prevent any further unauthorised excavation or construction at the site.Sources said AGEL has not yet complied with the stop-work order issued on Nov 13 by Satpute, in his capacity as the Satara division’s deputy conservator of forests, for starting work on the project without NBWL’s approval. Adani Group had earlier said the proposal had been submitted to NBWL. Satpute said he would need to check whether the developer had followed the order.
Article Summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd’s 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Forest department's honorary wildlife warden has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway.

Article Title: Buffs break away from fight, charge at 8-year-old boy, trample him to death in Ujjain
Article Text:
Eight-year-old boy named Yuvraj was killed by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain.





UJJAIN: In a tragic turn of events, an eight-year-old boy was trampled to death by charging buffaloes while watching a buffalo fight with his father on Friday. The incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain district.The buffalo fight, it turns out, is a traditional event held on the occasion of Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi, a calendar festival.The bout between two buffaloes was being staged in a field near the govt school. Around 2 pm, Akash arrived with his son Yuvraj to catch the fight. He stood at the edge of the crowd, while the boy sat close to him, eating poha (a popular local snack).As the buffaloes, released from their pen or enclosure, charged towards the spectators, one climbed onto Yuvraj’s chest. His father jumped to his rescue, and was joined by some bystanders who eventually helped pull the child out from under the marauding feet of the buffs.The boy was rushed to a hospital where the doctors declared him dead on arrival.Akash, a taxi driver, said Yuvraj, a Class 3 student, was his only son. “The buffaloes were in a fight and had locked horns. My son was sitting close to me as we watched the fight. However, all of a sudden, the buffaloes came charging in our direction and trampled my child,” the father said, laying the blame on the organiser.A private hospital in Chandesari declared him dead on arrival, after which his body was taken to the district hospital at Charak Bhawan, where a post-mortem was conducted before the last remains were handed to the family.Nagjhiri station in-charge Rakesh Bharti said such events are illegal, adding that the incident was being investigated. He said the organiser had been warned two days earlier and had promised not to hold the event, yet went ahead with it.A case of unnatural death was registered, the officer said, adding that a criminal case will be filed against the accused once the inquiry establishes the facts. Statements from the family are yet to be recorded.Local residents said a similar event three to four years ago had led to stone pelting at the police.
Article Summary: Eight-year-old trampled to death by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain. Incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s UJJain district.

Article Title: Rajasthan couple murdered by relative over vacating rented room
Article Text:
Couple killed by a distant relative following their request for him to leave his rental space





RAJKOT: A couple were killed and two of their relatives seriously injured when a distant relative of theirs attacked them with a nail-studded wooden club, as he held a grudge about being given notice to vacate the room they had rented to him, in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday.According to the FIR registered at Atkot police station on Friday, the deceased are Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35). The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodakiya (35), Prakash’s sister-in-law, and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew.Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Ghodakiya, a resident of the same village, on charges of murder.Talking to TOI, Jasdan assistant superintendent of police Naveen Chakravarthy Repudi said the accused was unemployed and had been given a room to stay by the victims. “When they asked him to vacate the room, he held a grudge about it. He later attacked them with a club which had nails in it, which caused grievous head injuries to the victims,” he said.According to Labhu’s complaint, around 3.30pm on Thursday, she had gone to Prakash’s house to bring back her young son, Vraj, There was a knock on the door and when. Vilas opened it they and saw Ashok — a distant cousin of Prakash’s — carrying a wooden club.He began hurling abuses.When Labhu and Vilas objected to his language, Ashok allegedly threatened to kill them and swung the club at Labhu’s head. She suffered an injury to her left palm while trying to block the first blow, before a second strike hit the left side of her head.When Vilas intervened to save Labhu, Ashok struck her repeatedly on the head with the club. Hearing their screams, Prakash rushed out, followed by Puri, who was sitting at a kirana shop behind the house. Both were allegedly hit on their heads until they collapsed.The accused fled after Labhu’s eldest brother-in-law, Ramesh, arrived. The two injured victims are getting treatment at a hospital.
Article Summary: Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35), were killed in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday. The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodkiya (35) and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew. Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Godakiya, on charges of murder.

Article Title: Bihar horror: Student dragged, molested; male friend assaulted, 3 arrested after video surfaces
Article Text:
Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student





PATNA: Police arrested three men within 12 hours of an incident in which a student was allegedly molested, assaulted and verbally abused in the Bochahan police station area of Muzaffarpur district.A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused.The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, son of Shivnath Sharma and a resident of Ward No. 1 in Kashirampur village; Vishal Kumar, son of Ram Kumar Sharma; and Ujjwal Kumar, son of Lal Babu Rai, a resident of Bhorhan village. All three were taken to Bochahan police station for questioning before being formally booked in the case.Alay Vats, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (East-I), said the incident came to light on November 19 after the video surfaced on social media."In the video, the accused molested the girl and indulged in indecent behaviour, while her friend was assaulted. Taking the matter seriously, officers began verifying the footage, examined the circumstances of the incident and identified those involved. Following the investigation and verification of the location, a police team conducted raids and apprehended all three accused within 12 hours," he said.Police also seized two mobile phones allegedly used to record and circulate the video. An FIR was registered under relevant sections of the law, and the process of sending the arrested men to judicial custody was initiated.Bochahan SHO Yashwant Kumar Mishra said police acted immediately after receiving information about the incident and intensified efforts to identify and arrest the accused. He confirmed that three men had been arrested, two mobile phones seized and further investigation was under way.The arrests were made by a team from Bochahan police station under the supervision of SDPO East-I, with the SHO leading the operation.
Article Summary: Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student. A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused. The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, Vishal Kumar and Ujjwal Kumar.

Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions

Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph

PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their sentiments, while insisting that she had no intention of disrespecting him.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.
