Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'
Article Text:
The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December

Death sentence and legal proceedings

Political implications of her return

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Bangladesh extradite Sheikh Hasina back from India? Yes, to face justice No, she should remain in India Only if the legal process permits I don't have enough information 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: Russian drone strike collapses apartment building in Kyiv region, 14 feared trapped
Article Text:
A street cleaner looks at damage to the site of a warehouse that was struck during a Russian drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine, November 20

Russian attacks deepen crisis in Kyiv

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At least 14 people may be trapped under the rubble of a residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region after a Russian drone struck it on Sunday morning, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Nine people have been evacuated from the damaged five-storey building, while emergency teams continue search and rescue operations. Two people, including a teenager, were injured, local officials said."Part of a five-storey apartment building has collapsed following a Russian drone attack. I thank our first responders for acting quickly: nine people have already been evacuated, and the fire has been contained," Zelenskyy said on X.Footage released by emergency services showed rescuers searching through a large pile of rubble. Some residents were helped out of the damaged building using ladders and a crane platform.The attack came amid continued drone strikes between Russia and Ukraine. In Russia, five people were injured in overnight Ukrainian drone attacks on the Krasnodar region, Russian media reported on Sunday.State news agency TASS, citing regional authorities, said four of the injured were in the village of Afipsky. The village is home to an oil refinery that has been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian forces in recent months.The latest attack comes as Kyiv faces increasingly frequent Russian strikes, which have worsened security conditions and disrupted daily life in the Ukrainian capital.Since September, Russia has stepped up attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas, targeting infrastructure, including power facilities, railway stations, roads and shopping centres.The deteriorating situation has also hit businesses, particularly restaurants and cafes, as residents avoid the city centre amid frequent air raid alerts.In September and October, Kyiv recorded 437 hours of air alerts. With sirens sounding for long periods, many residents have chosen to stay home rather than visit restaurants and other public spaces.Several hospitality businesses have shut down or suspended operations until the end of winter. Restaurant chain Gastro Family has closed two outlets in Kyiv and suspended operations at two others until April, its owner Olena Borysova told Reuters.Chornomorka, a seafood restaurant chain, has reported a roughly 20 per cent drop in customer visits compared with last year. The company has closed two restaurants in Kyiv and plans to relocate them to western Ukraine."It's not about earning or making any profit," the chain's development director Dmytro Kostrubin said. "The lucky one is the one who can break even."The crisis has also affected other restaurant groups. Pesto Cafe temporarily closed seven of its 20 restaurants in Kyiv and the surrounding region because of frequent air raids and worsening security conditions.According to Ukraine's National Restaurant Association, the country's restaurant sector employs around 150,000 people and generated about 248 billion hryvnias ($5 billion) in sales last year.Restaurant owners have tried to adapt by installing generators and water tanks to deal with power and water cuts. Some have also developed menus that can be prepared without electricity or running water.However, rising costs, staff shortages, curfews and falling consumer spending have made it increasingly difficult for businesses to remain operational.Annual inflation reached 11 per cent in October, putting further pressure on household budgets. Restaurant owners have reported that customers are spending less, often cutting out additional drinks and desserts.Borysova said the average order at her restaurants had fallen from three items to two as customers became more cautious about spending.
Article Summary: At least 14 people may be trapped under the rubble of a residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region after a Russian drone struck it on Sunday morning. Nine people have been evacuated from the damaged five-storey building, while emergency teams continue search and rescue operations. Two people, including a teenager, were injured.

Article Title: ‘Not everything can happen during elections’: Why Ladakh’s MHA dialogue is on hold till Dec 4
Article Text:
“The voter turnout percentage and the fact that people have participated in such large numbers, is a testament to the fact that people in Ladakh want democracy,” Kundra said.





SRINAGAR: The Ladakh administration on Sunday welcomed the high voter turnout in the panchayat and municipal elections held on Saturday, saying it reflected people's desire for democracy.Appealing to residents to participate in large numbers in the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections scheduled for December 4, Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra said talks between leaders of the region and the ministry of home affairs (MHA) would resume after the polls.Addressing a press conference in Leh, Kundra said negotiations should continue and parties should not outrightly reject proposals on the table.He asserted that the government of India was committed to providing the best possible solution under Article 371 for the people of Ladakh. He also urged Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk not to make what he called provocative statements during the election season.“The voter turnout percentage and the fact that people have participated in such large numbers, is a testament to the fact that people in Ladakh want democracy,” Kundra said.Ladakh recorded a 70.03% turnout in the panchayat elections and 52.4% in the municipal council polls on Saturday. “We must not forget that the last panchayat and municipal elections were held in 2018. This is the first time elections are being held since Ladakh became a Union Territory,” he said.On talks between the MHA and Ladakh leaders represented by the Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), Kundra said the dialogue would resume soon after the election process was over.“The dialogue between the ministry of home affairs and the political leadership is a political dialogue. Anything that could influence the outcome of elections cannot be undertaken during the election process,” he said.Kundra said he had personally conveyed to Chering Dorjay Lakrook, co-chairman of the LAB, on two occasions that the MHA would resume political dialogue on the larger structure or body under discussion once the elections were over.He indicated that elected representatives could also be included in the talks alongside the LAB and KDA.“We are not saying that talks with the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance will come to an end (after the polls). But those who are elected as representatives are also the voice of the people and they will have to be brought into the dialogue also,” he said.However, he added: “It is incorrect to suggest, as some statements appear to imply, that we will speak only to the elected representatives and leave the LAB and KDA out of the process. Such statements are misleading and create confusion.”Kundra also said a maximalist position should be avoided during negotiations and that dialogue should not be discontinued.“One should never outrightly reject what is on the table. In any kind of negotiation a few things are required. First, mutual trust. Second, a process of give and take. I cannot adopt a maximalist position and say that I want this and only this. We have to accommodate each other,” he said.He reiterated that within the framework of the Constitution of India, the government was committed to providing the best possible solution under Article 371 to Ladakh.Asked about the LAB's demand to defer the LAHDC elections, Kundra said, “Only 10 to 12 days are left for the elections and around 70% of the people have already voted in the Panchayat election. So at this stage, to claim that 40% of the people are not even here is not correct. It is not as if people are casting their votes without being present.”On the demand for polling booths in Srinagar and Jammu for Ladakh residents currently in these cities, he said it would not be possible to arrange them as polling stations had already been frozen.However, he said special arrangements could be explored for those currently outside Ladakh, including facilitating travel through Sadbhavana flights.“I would have no objection to it. But we will have to speak to the Air Force authorities to explore whether special flights can be arranged so that anyone who wishes to vote can travel to Ladakh, cast their vote and then move back,” he said.
Article Summary: Ladakh recorded a 70.03% turnout in the panchayat elections and 52.4% in the municipal council polls on Saturday. Chief secretary Ashish Kundra said talks between leaders of the region and the ministry of home affairs would resume after the polls. He urged Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk not to make what he called provocative statements during the election season.

Article Title: UK man jailed for life after drowning ex-Microsoft executive at private members’ club in drug-fuelled murder
Article Text:
Nelio Gouveia/Image: Thames Valley Police

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A former Microsoft executive was killed after a man struck her repeatedly with a metal weight-lifting bar before holding her underwater in the River Thames at a private members’ club in Oxfordshire.Nelio Gouveia, 45, was handed a life sentence at Oxford Crown Court for killing Jennifer Symonds, 44, at Phyllis Court club in Henley-on-Thames in March. He will serve a minimum of 22 years and six months in prison, The Independent reportedThe court heard that Gouveia, who worked as a kitchen porter at the club, had arranged to meet Symonds on 5 March. They spent the evening visiting pubs and consuming alcohol and drugs before going to his room at the venue. A club member later reported hearing a man shouting “I love you”, followed by a woman screaming.The attack took place after Gouveia left Symonds near a pavilion. He visited a pornographic website before returning to his room to collect a metal weight-lifting bar. Concealing the weapon in the back of his trousers, he went back to the riverside, where Symonds was waiting.Gouveia hit her over the head three or four times, causing them to fall against a boat moored nearby and into the river, prosecutor Neil Moore told the court.He then prevented Symonds from reaching the surface, pushing her head underwater with his hands while using his feet to keep her submerged. Moore said the assault continued for approximately 12 minutes.“Jennifer Symonds fought desperately to cling on to her life,” the prosecutor said, adding that Gouveia became more determined to keep her underwater as she struggled.Gouveia pleaded guilty to the murder last month. The incident was recorded by CCTV cameras, although the footage was not played during the hearing. Mr Justice Jay described the recording as “deeply disturbing and upsetting”.The sentencing hearing also examined Gouveia’s history of violence against women. He had been given a suspended prison sentence for attacking another woman in June 2022 and was still serving that sentence when Symonds was killed. During the earlier incident, he punched the woman in the face and struck her with a wine bottle at a gathering.Mr Justice Jay said the similarities between the two assaults were “disturbing”. He described Gouveia as having a propensity for violence towards women, saying excessive drug and alcohol consumption had fuelled his behaviour during the murder.The judge also referred to Gouveia’s “appetite for violent pornography” and said the killing represented an “exercise of power and desire to dominate”. He further described the removal of some of Symonds’s clothing as an act of “humiliation and degradation”.Prosecutors raised the possibility that Gouveia attacked Symonds because she had rejected a sexual advance. However, the judge said this remained a possible explanation rather than something established to the criminal standard.Symonds had built a career in the technology industry and worked at Microsoft before being made redundant the year before her death. She was born in Zambia and moved to the UK at the age of three. After studying at the University of Gloucestershire, she went on to work in IT and received several professional awards, the court heard.Her family spoke about the loss during the proceedings. Her brother, Andrew Symonds, said she was “deeply missed every day” and remembered her as a kind and caring person who had affected the lives of many people.Her father, Peter Symonds, described the family's trauma as “devastating”. He said he continued to be haunted by what his daughter had suffered before her death and urged the judge to “please protect other women for as long as possible”.Following the murder, Gouveia travelled by taxi to Heathrow Airport, intending to fly to Latvia. He subsequently returned to Henley and went to a police station, where he told officers: “I think I hurt someone. I think I may have killed someone and I need to speak to someone quickly.”He was arrested on the day Symonds’s body was discovered in the Thames.
Article Summary: Nelio Gouveia, 45, was handed a life sentence at Oxford Crown Court. He killed Jennifer Symonds, 44, at Phyllis Court club in Henley-on-Thames in March. He will serve a minimum of 22 years and six months in prison.

Article Title: 'I want a Brezza': Bride's family gifts Delhi cop Hyundai Aura, he calls it a 'taxi', leaves her waiting at mandap
Article Text:
The groom, Kuldeep (L), bride's family(R)

The wedding invitation card





SONIPAT: A wedding in Sonipat turned into a controversy after a Delhi Police personnel allegedly refused to proceed with the marriage over a dispute concerning the car arranged by the bride’s family.The groom, Kuldeep, allegedly insisted on a Maruti Suzuki Brezza instead of the Hyundai Aura booked by the bride’s family, reportedly describing the latter as a vehicle commonly used as a taxi.Following the disagreement, he returned with around 30 members of the wedding party, leaving the bride waiting at the mandap in her wedding attire.According to a complaint filed by the bride’s father, Subhash Kumar, a resident of the Ram Nagar area, his daughter Hina’s marriage had been fixed with Kuldeep, a resident of Gandhi Nagar in Gohana, around six months ago.Both families had mutually agreed to solemnise the marriage on November 20, following which the family began preparations and sent invitations to relatives.Subhash alleged that the issue of a car came up on November 19, a day before the wedding. His family was scheduled to visit the groom’s house for the engagement ceremony. Before the visit, he received a phone call from Anil and Rajesh, who had helped arrange the marriage.During the conversation, Anil allegedly asked whether the bride’s family had arranged a car for the wedding. Subhash said he had already booked a vehicle for the groom.However, Anil subsequently informed him that Kuldeep was not satisfied with the Hyundai Aura booked for him. The groom allegedly said that the model was commonly used as a taxi and that he wanted a Brezza instead.The bride’s father claimed that he cancelled the booking of the Aura, which was worth approximately Rs 9.5 lakh, and approached several dealers in Sonipat and nearby areas to arrange a Brezza. However, with very little time left before the wedding, he could not arrange the vehicle. He also claimed that the groom’s family later spoke about arranging a car from Narnaund.In his complaint, Subhash alleged that his family had made arrangements to gift Kuldeep a two-tola gold chain, his mother four-tola gold earrings and a silver anklet. Jewellery was also planned for the groom’s elder brother and sister-in-law.Besides this, good-quality furniture and other household items had been prepared for the groom, involving an expenditure of around Rs 1.32 lakh.The family had booked Mamchand Vatika for the wedding and arranged food for approximately 1,200 guests. Subhash claimed that the family had spent between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 30 lakh on the wedding preparations.According to the complainant, on November 20, when the Brezza could not be arranged, Kuldeep arrived at the wedding venue in ordinary clothes along with his mother instead of proceeding with the customary wedding ceremonies.Subhash alleged that members of the groom’s family abused the bride’s relatives. He further claimed that Kuldeep’s sister-in-law, while identifying herself as an advocate, threatened to take them to court. Kuldeep allegedly invoked his position in Delhi Police during the confrontation.Following the altercation, the groom left the venue with around 30 members of the wedding party. The incident left Hina waiting at the mandap in her bridal attire as the marriage ceremony remained incomplete.Subhash said his daughter Hina had completed her MA and JBT qualifications, while Kuldeep had studied up to Class XII. He alleged that at the time of finalising the alliance, the groom’s family had assured them that they would neither make any demands nor accept dowry. However, demands concerning a car and jewellery allegedly surfaced around the wedding.After the baraat left, Subhash called the emergency helpline 112 to inform the police. The groom’s side also reportedly contacted the helpline. Subsequently, the bride’s family approached Sector 27 police station and submitted a complaint seeking action against Kuldeep and his family.Sector 27 police station SHO Savit Kumar said the police had received a complaint from the bride’s family and had called both parties to the police station.“Both parties have been called, and discussions are currently underway. We will see what decision emerges from the discussions, following which further action will be taken,” he said.
Article Summary: The groom, Kuldeep, allegedly insisted on a Maruti Suzuki Brezza instead of the Hyundai Aura booked by the bride’s family. He reportedly described the latter as a vehicle commonly used as a taxi. Following the disagreement, he returned with around 30 members of the wedding party, leaving the bride waiting at the mandap.

Article Title: LSR hosts VU Amsterdam delegation, signs academic collaboration pact
Article Text:
Prof Kanika K Ahuja and Dr Margrethe Jonkman with LSR staff and students





Lady Shri Ram College for Women, DU hosted a high-level delegation from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, led by President Dr Margrethe Jonkman, on 17 November 2026. The visit culminated in the signing of an MoU between LSR and VU Amsterdam, providing a framework for student exchange, short-term courses, joint research, research supervision, and visiting faculty.Principal Prof. Kanika K. Ahuja described the MoU as an “opening of horizons” and an opportunity to become part of a larger intellectual commons through collaborative inquiry and shared scholarship.Dr Margrethe Jonkman spoke about the meaning of Vrije, which translates to freedom, and highlighted the importance of mutual learning through academic exchange and science diplomacy. Discussions between the delegations focused on faculty mobility, collaborative research and community service learning. Proposed areas of research included everyday life through the ages, gender and art in India, and indigenous knowledge texts.Two student programmes were outlined during discussions, the Women Leading Change Summer School in Amsterdam in July 2027, and Autumn School organized by LSR for students of VU in October 2027. The visit concluded with a campus tour led by LSR students.
Article Summary: Lady Shri Ram College for Women, DU hosted a high-level delegation from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. The visit culminated in the signing of an MoU between LSR and VU Amsterdam. Proposed areas of research included everyday life through the ages, gender and art in India, and indigenous knowledge texts.

Article Title: 8 rescued after fire breaks out at Mumbai central building
Article Text:
A fire broke out in the Hira Manzil building in Mumbai Central shortly after midnight. Eight people, including an elderly woman and two children, were rescued





MUMBAI: At least eight people, including an elderly woman and two children, were rescued after a fire broke out in a residential building on Gildar Lane near Reliance Supermarket in Mumbai Central, shortly after midnight on Sunday.The fire was reported to the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) at 12.07 am at Hira Manzil, a ground-plus-three-storey building. The blaze spread through a room on the second floor, gutting electrical wiring, furniture and household articles.Three people — a man and two women — were rescued from the third floor using a turntable ladder (TTL), while an elderly woman was brought out from the first floor via the staircase.Four others — a man, a woman, a boy and a girl — were rescued from a room on the fourth floor using the staircase, according to the fire brigade.The fire was classified as Level I at 12.23 am and escalated to Level II at 12.50 am. Firefighters managed to extinguish it at 5.05 am.The blaze damaged electrical installations, wooden furniture, partitions, cupboards, beds, doors, windows, ceiling fans, a split air conditioner, a television, papers, documents and other household articles.The elderly woman rescued from the first floor was taken to HN Reliance Hospital in a police van.She was treated in the casualty ward and discharged.A senior station officer from Memonwada Fire Station sustained a cut injury to his right palm while fighting the fire. He was taken to Nair Hospital in a 108 ambulance, where he received stitches and was discharged.Fire brigade personnel, including officers and firefighters, along with a turntable ladder, an ambulance and other equipment, were deployed at the site. No other injuries were reported.
Article Summary: A fire broke out in a residential building on Gildar Lane near Reliance Supermarket in Mumbai Central, shortly after midnight on Sunday. The fire was reported to the Mumbai Fire Brigade at 12.07 am at Hira Manzil, a ground-plus- three-storey building. The blaze spread through a room on the second floor, gutting electrical wiring, furniture and household articles.

Article Title: Latur police register 8 cases over noise pollution violations, seize sound systems worth Rs 8.5 lakh
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: Latur police have registered cases against eight people for violating prescribed noise pollution limits during processions held to mark Hazrat Tipu Sultan birth anniversary on Friday.Police also seized three vehicles fitted with high-powered sound systems worth an estimated Rs 8.5 lakh after detecting unauthorised modifications.Of the eight cases, four were registered at MIDC police station, three at Vivekanand Chowk police station, and one at Shivajinagar police station, said Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe.Sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) Sameersinh Salve said police teams used sound-level measuring devices to monitor noise during the processions. They recorded sound intensity and collected readings to establish violations before initiating legal action against those found using loudspeakers and sound systems beyond permissible limits.In a separate action, MIDC police seized three vehicles fitted with high-capacity sound systems after detecting unauthorised modifications. The equipment installed in the vehicles is estimated to be worth Rs 8.5 lakh.Proposals are being sent to the Regional Transport Office (RTO) for further penal and legal action against the vehicle owners.SP Tambe said police have consistently been creating awareness about the harmful effects of noise pollution and urging organisers to adhere to prescribed limits during religious, social, and public events.“Police have been appealing to mandals, organisers, and citizens through peace committee meetings and social media campaigns to ensure that noise pollution norms are followed during processions and public celebrations. While several mandals have responded positively, strict legal action will be taken against those who continue to violate the prescribed limits despite repeated appeals. There will be no compromise on noise pollution,” Tambe said.He added that excessive noise adversely affects senior citizens, infants, pregnant women, and patients, besides disturbing the daily lives of other residents.Police have equipped several stations in the district with sound-measuring devices to monitor noise levels during major festivals, anniversaries, and public gatherings. Tambe appealed to citizens and event organisers to exercise social responsibility and cooperate with the police in keeping Latur free from noise pollution.
Article Summary: Latur police have registered cases against eight people for violating noise pollution limits during processions held to mark Hazrat Tipu Sultan birth anniversary. Police also seized three vehicles fitted with high-powered sound systems worth an estimated Rs 8.5 lakh after detecting unauthorised modifications.

Article Title: Latur police book 80 in district-wide illegal liquor crackdown
Article Text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:The Latur police registered 80 cases and initiated action against 80 people during a district-wide crackdown on the illegal liquor trade on Thursday. The special drive was conducted simultaneously across all 23 police station jurisdictions in the district on November 20.Police seized liquor and other materials collectively valued at Rs 3.81 lakh during the operation.Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe said the drive involved 152 police personnel, including 25 officers and 127 constables and other personnel. Teams were deployed across the district to identify and raid locations where illegal liquor was being sold.Tambe said that he had directed police officials to sustain action against illegal activities, including the sale of illicit liquor, gambling and matka operations.Apart from registering cases, the police are also initiating preventive action against those involved in such activities. The offenders are required to execute legal bonds undertaking not to repeat the offences. Those found violating these conditions and resuming illegal activities will face further stringent legal action.The police said the objective was not merely to book offenders but also to deter them from returning to illegal activities and prevent the recurrence of such businesses.Similar special drives will continue across the district to curb illegal activities and maintain law and order, police said.
Article Summary: The Latur police registered 80 cases and initiated action against 80 people during a district-wide crackdown on the illegal liquor trade on Thursday. The special drive was conducted simultaneously across all 23 police station jurisdictions in the district on November 20. Police seized liquor and other materials collectively valued at Rs 3.81 lakh during the operation.

Article Title: Fugitive deported from UAE in exploitation case remanded in 14-day police custody
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A man wanted in a case of alleged sexual exploitation and financial fraud on the pretext of marriage, who was brought back from Dubai in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city police’s first such international operation, was remanded in police custody for 14 days by a local court on Saturday.Mohammed Mazin Mohammed Abdul Rashid was traced and apprehended in Dubai with the assistance of INTERPOL and UAE authorities before being brought to India on Nov 19. Police said his interrogation was underway and investigators were probing whether he was involved in more cases of alleged fraud and exploitation.DCP (Zone I) Pankaj Atulkar said the operation marked the first time the city police had brought a wanted accused back from abroad.“The accused should not think that he can commit an offence, flee abroad and escape the law. Our reach extends beyond borders, and we can bring an accused back even from across seven seas,” Atulkar said.The case was registered at City Chowk police station on Dec 1, 2025, following a woman’s complaint alleging that Mazin had promised to marry her, established physical relations with her and subsequently cheated her of money.Police said their investigation had also uncovered alleged financial fraud involving two other women and a man. Atulkar said the amount allegedly cheated from three victims totalled Rs 19.7 lakh.Mazin has been booked under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. His mother and sister were also initially named in the case but were subsequently served notices and released, police said.ACP Sagar Deshmukh said Maharashtra Police, the state CID, home department, CBI, INTERPOL and UAE authorities coordinated to bring Mazin back. A lookout notice was issued after he left India following registration of the case, and a Red Corner Notice was subsequently issued to facilitate his tracing and apprehension abroad.“The entire process took around one-and-a-half months. However, our team travelled to Dubai and completed the necessary procedures to take him into custody within three days. Coordination with the agencies concerned and completion of legal formalities were crucial to bringing him back,” Deshmukh said.In an earlier statement, CBI had said the principal complainant was allegedly cheated of Rs 18 lakh. The agency had also alleged that Mazin exploited 13 other women on the pretext of marriage, collected money from them and recorded videos of intimate acts. CBI had said a chargesheet was filed before the competent court. These allegations form part of the wider investigation.Assistant inspector Manoj Shinde said Mazin was brought to India and subsequently taken into custody by the city police team. His interrogation is underway, with police examining whether further cases of alleged financial fraud and exploitation could emerge.Police commissioner Pravin Pawar appealed to women facing fraud, sexual exploitation or harassment on the pretext of marriage to approach police without fear or concern over social pressure.
Article Summary: Mohammed Mazin Mohammed Abdul Rashid was traced and apprehended in Dubai with the assistance of INTERPOL and UAE authorities. Police said his interrogation was underway and investigators were probing whether he was involved in more cases of alleged fraud and exploitation. The case was registered at City Chowk police station on Dec 1, 2025.

Article Title: HC suspends gangster Mehandi's life term in Shaikh Naser murder case
Article Text:
Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court on Thursday suspended the life sentence of gangster Shaikh Imran Mehandi alias Dilawar in the 2011 murder of Shaikh Naser Shaikh Chand during the pendency of his appeal, citing that convicting a person merely on recovery of a knife was “dangerous”.This is the third murder case, apart from the Salim Qureshi and Sirajuddin Ansari murder cases, in which Mehandi has secured bail. He is unlikely to walk out of jail soon, though. His bail applications and pleas for suspension of sentence are pending in at least two more murder cases.A division bench of Justice Sandipkumar More and Justice Vaishali Patil-Jadhav directed Mehandi’s release on a PR bond of Rs25,000 with one surety of the same amount, “if not required in any other case”.A special MCOCA court on Aug 1, 2018, convicted Mehandi and accused number 5 Syed Jahir alias Shera Bakhar Qureshi of murdering Shaikh Naser. It sentenced them to life imprisonment, while acquitting five others. Mehandi’s appeal is pending before the high court.According to the prosecution, Naser was killed on Sept 9, 2011, through sedative-laced juice, strangulation and knife blows, and his body was buried at Irfan Farm House in Savangi.The FIR was lodged at Begumpura police station in March 2012.Mehandi’s counsel, advocate Rupesh Jaiswal, argued there was no direct or last-seen evidence and that Mehandi’s name surfaced only after Jahir’s disclosure statement, with the conviction resting solely on a knife recovery.The division bench of the high court noted that Naser’s body was exhumed seven months after burial and that the knife was recovered from an open place accessible to all. Convicting a person merely on its recovery was “dangerous”, it said, and the prosecution had to establish a complete chain of circumstances.The court accepted that “there is no presumption of innocence of the accused at the stage of post-conviction” and suspension in Section 302 cases “is an exception and not the rule”. But it said “in the instant case, considering that conviction of the applicant is based only on recovery of the knife at his instance, there is a good scope for him to succeed in the appeal”. The appeal, recently filed, was unlikely to be heard soon, the high court said.The court ordered that the life sentence imposed on Aug 1, 2018, “is hereby suspended during the pendency of this appeal”. It clarified that its observations would not affect the merits of the appeal.On Sept 15, Supreme Court had suspended Mehandi’s life sentence in the 2012 murder of former corporator Salim Qureshi. Besides the pending bail pleas in at least two more murder cases, he faces trials in Nilesh Mhatre, Sindubai Mhatre and Sirajuddin murder cases, all registered in 2012.
Article Summary: Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court suspends the life sentence of gangster Shaikh Imran Mehandi alias Dilawar in the 2011 murder of Shaikh Naser Shaikh Chand. A division bench of Justice Sandipkumar More and Justice Vaishali Patil- Jadhav directed Me handi’s release on a PR bond of Rs25,000 with one surety.

Article Title: Sarpanch’s son drowns in Padmavati dam after fixing village water pipeline
Article Text:
The victim’s body was recovered from the dam with the assistance of a National Disaster Response Force team

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 25-year-old man, son of the sarpanch of Masrul village in Buldhana district, drowned in Padmavati dam in Bhokardan taluka of Jalna district while swimming back to the shore after completing work on the village water supply pipeline on Thursday.The deceased was identified as Madhukar Mahale. Paradh police of Jalna district registered a case of accidental death.Madhukar is survived by his mother, wife, two daughters and a son. His father, Shakuntalabai Mahale, is the sarpanch of Masrul village on the border of Buldhana and Jalna districts.Padmavati dam is on the border of the two districts. It had been the source of water for several neighbouring villages in both the districts, said Jalna superintendent of police Teghbir Singh Sandhu.The water from this dam has a pipeline connected to a well that caters to Masrul villagers. The water pump and the pipeline had developed a snag. The victim, Madhukar, along with a gram panchayat member, went to the dam and swam their way to the water pump.Paradh’s assistant inspector Sachin Khamgal, citing the eyewitnesses’ statement, said Madhukar had gone to the dam around 2.30pm with the gram panchayat member, K K Sinkar, to connect the pipeline to a public well in the dam’s submerged area.The well is part of the water supply scheme through which Padmavati dam water reaches Masrul village.After completing the work, the two attempted to swim back to the shore. Madhukar was exhausted midway and drowned. Sinkar managed to reach the shore and alerted villagers, following which a search and rescue operation was launched.Disaster management officer Sambhaji Pawar reached the spot with a rescue team. After an intensive search lasting around three hours, Madhukar’s body was recovered from the dam with the assistance of a National Disaster Response Force team.His body was taken to a Dhad-based state medical facility late on Thursday. An autopsy was performed on Friday morning before the body was handed over to Madhukar’s family members. His last rites were performed in the afternoon.Madhukar was known for taking an active role in addressing villagers’ problems. His death while working on the village’s water supply project plunged Masrul into mourning, said Balu Patil, a resident of the village.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Madhukar Mahale. He is the son of the sarpanch of Masrul village in Buldhana district. The water pump and the pipeline had developed a snag. The victim and a gram panchayat member went to the dam and swam their way to the water pump. After completing the work, the two attempted to swim back to the shore.

Article Title: ​4 eateries, sweet units shut in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar after FDA crackdown
Article Text:
One of the food units raided by FDA

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has ordered the immediate shutdown of four food units in the district after inspections uncovered filthy kitchens, uncovered food, chemicals stored with edibles, and serious hygiene lapses.Conducted on Nov 18 under the Safe Food Safe Maharashtra campaign, the crackdown led Assistant Commissioner (Food) D V Patil to suspend the licenses and registrations of all four establishments under Section 32(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.“All four units have been directed to stop food business, production and sale till further orders. The suspension will be lifted only after the deficiencies are rectified and a re-inspection finds satisfactory improvement,” Patil said.A hotel at Tisgaon in CIDCO Waluj Mahanagar scored 34/102 during a complaint-based inspection that revealed broken floor tiles, a blackened ceiling, no drainage, irregular garbage disposal, no drinking water test report, no pest control, and no temperature records for hot and cold storage.A sweet manufacturing unit on Khadi Road in Devlai scored 26/64 in a complaint-based check, with officials citing poor ventilation, food and chemicals stored together, no pest control, improper waste disposal, workers without protective clothing, and poor cleanliness.A cold drink and pedha centre at Vasadi in Kannad scored 30/62. Inspectors reported dust and dirt on the floor, smoke-blackened walls, pedhas kept in the open, staff handling food without aprons, gloves or head covers, and missing medical and training certificates for staff.A sweet mart at Vasadi in Kannad scored 44/78. Registered only as a hawker but manufacturing food, the outlet had an open backyard kitchen with food particles scattered on the floor, missing pest control records, and no water or food testing reports.FDA joint commissioner (food) Shrikaant Karkale said food business operators must strictly follow hygiene norms. “If any violations are found, stringent action will follow in the light of laid down rules and regulations in a larger public interest,” he said.
Article Summary: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) orders immediate shutdown of four food units in the district. Inspectors uncovered filthy kitchens, uncovered food, chemicals stored with edibles, and serious hygiene lapses. All four units have been directed to stop food business, production and sale till further orders.

Article Title: ​Health campaign ‘Arogyam 2026’ organised in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar till Nov 24 on occasion of Prakash Gurpurab
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Khalsa Foundation is organising ‘Arogyam 2026’, a special health service campaign, in different parts of the city till Nov 24 to mark the Prakash Gurpurab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the birth anniversary of the founder of Sikhism.Foundation secretary Sardar Sarbjit Singh said expert doctors, hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres will provide free medical consultation, select health check-ups and diagnostic tests at special discounted rates. “The services will include general health consultation, paediatrics, gynaecology, dentistry, ear, nose and throat (ENT) tests, cardiac check-ups and select diagnostic and imaging services,” he said.A special eye check-up camp ‘Drishti’ will also be organised in collaboration with Lions Eye Hospital, Chikalthana, on Saturday at Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, Guru Gobind Singh Pura. The camp will provide eye check-up facilities, especially for senior citizens, children and people with vision complaints. Guidance on Ayushman Card, its registration process and other govt health schemes will also be provided to citizens.Khalsa Foundation has appealed to citizens of all religions, castes and communities in the city and surrounding areas to avail of the campaign. For registration and more information, citizens can contact 8446995333 / 9823561111.Foundation president Sardar Rajwinder Singh Dhodi said the campaign aims to make essential healthcare accessible and affordable for all sections of society while creating awareness about preventive health check-ups.“It is based on the values of seva, compassion, equality and ‘Sarbat Da Bhala’ - welfare of all, preached and practised by Guru Nanak Dev Ji,” he said.
Article Summary: Khalsa Foundation is organising ‘Arogyam 2026’ to mark the Prakash Gurpurab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the birth anniversary of the founder of Sikhism. Experts will provide free medical consultation, select health check-ups and diagnostic tests at special discounted rates.
